claim.pdf_says: 14.9.11.4   General rules  (bold run-in heading, one level below '14.9.11 DISPLAY statement', at the same level as 14.9.11.1 General, 14.9.11.2 General formats and 14.9.11.3 Syntax rules)
claim.markdown_says: ## 14.9.11.4 General rules   (H2 - while its siblings on the preceding pages are '### 14.9.11.1 General', '### 14.9.11.2 General formats', '### 14.9.11.3 Syntax rules', and its parent is '## 14.9.11 DISPLAY statement')
claim.why_it_matters: At H2 the General rules subsection becomes a SIBLING of the statement it belongs to instead of a child, so the document outline/TOC detaches every DISPLAY general rule from the DISPLAY statement. The file's own convention elsewhere (e.g. 14.9.9.1-.4, 14.9.15.1-.4) is '## 14.9.N <statement>' with '### 14.9.N.M <subsection>'.
claim.reported_kind_is_wrong: Nothing is missing. The heading, its clause number and its title are all present and verbatim correct. The claim is about markdown heading DEPTH, not about absent text.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on two independent grounds. (1) THE PDF DOES NOT ENCODE HEADING LEVEL AT ALL, so there is nothing for the markdown to contradict. I rendered page 640 (the immediately preceding page, which carries the sibling headings) and page 641 at 300 dpi and compared the printed glyphs. On p640, '14.9.11 DISPLAY statement', '14.9.11.1 General', '14.9.11.2 General formats' and '14.9.11.3 Syntax rules' are set in IDENTICAL typography - same bold face, same point size, same left margin, same vertical spacing. The three-level PARENT is typographically indistinguishable from its four-level CHILDREN. On p641, '14.9.11.4 General rules' is set in that same one bold style. ISO conveys the hierarchy of this document SOLELY through the dotted clause number; it uses no size or weight gradation. The claim's premise - that the PDF 'says' 14.9.11.4 sits 'one level below 14.9.11' and 'at the same level as 14.9.11.1' - is an inference the reader draws from the digits '14.9.11.4', not something the page prints. The markdown carries those exact digits. Every hierarchical fact the PDF states is therefore preserved intact; the '#' count is transcription furniture the source does not specify. (2) IT IS NOT A PAGE-641 DEFECT; IT IS A DOCUMENT-WIDE NORMALIZATION ARTIFACT. Across the whole of specs/ISO_COBOL.md, 162 four-level headings are emitted at '##' and 620 at '###'. The '##' cases run from clause 6 to clause 14 and beyond - '## 6.2.3.2 Syntax rules', '## 7.3.7.1 General', '## 8.3.3.3 Numeric literals', '## 14.9.1.3', '## 14.9.2.4', '## 14.9.10.4', '## 14.9.12.4', '## 14.9.13.3', '## 14.9.22.4', '## 14.9.28.4', '## 14.9.40.4' and many more. The three-level headings wobble too: '### 14.9.1 ACCEPT statement' sits at H3 while '## 14.9.2 ADD statement' sits at H2. So the claim's supporting assertion - that '## 14.9.N / ### 14.9.N.M' is 'the file's own convention' - is contradicted by 162 counterexamples; the two examples it cites (14.9.9, 14.9.15) are cherry-picked from the majority side of an inconsistent pipeline. Flagging p641 as a structural discrepancy of THIS page misattributes a global markdown-generator quirk to a specific page of the source. No word, number, rule or piece of normative content differs between the PDF page and the transcription. I diffed the page body line by line: FORMAT 2 syntax rule 3, the heading, FORMAT 1, and general rules 1-9 including sub-items 5a and 5b all transcribe faithfully. Any citation of '14.9.11.4' resolves to the correct text, and the file's own '' anchor (present on the line above the heading) makes the section addressable regardless of '#' count. Per the rejection criteria this is 'only ... formatting' and 'does not change meaning'.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-to-markdown discrepancy. The heading '14.9.11.4 General rules' is present and verbatim correct at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 26541, preceded by anchor ''. The PDF makes NO typographic distinction between 14.9.11 (parent) and 14.9.11.1-.4 (children) - all five are the same bold face at the same size and margin - so the PDF never states a heading level for the markdown to lose; hierarchy lives in the clause number, which is transcribed exactly. Separately, the markdown-internal '#'-depth inconsistency is genuine but global and cosmetic: 162 of 782 four-level headings across the file are at H2 rather than H3 (and some three-level headings, e.g. '### 14.9.1 ACCEPT statement', are at H3 rather than H2). If that is worth fixing, it belongs in a single document-wide heading-depth normalization pass over the transcription pipeline, filed once - NOT as a per-page spec-reconciliation finding against page 641, and not at severity 'structural' against the ISO source.
